te: Policy on granting and revoking Thai nationality and national security
se: Meeting on Wednesday 23 September 2026 at 13.30 in committee meeting room CA 428, 4th floor, Parliament House, according to the meeting notice. The agenda is following the policy and practice of granting and revoking Thai nationality to prevent threats to national security in various dimensions, with representatives of the Ministry of Interior and the Office of the National Security Council invited. (The Senate has published only the meeting notice; there is no meeting summary yet.)
it: Policy and practice of granting and revoking Thai nationality

te: China's role in the Mekong subregion (National Security Council)
se: A representative of the National Security Council said the Mekong subregion is a strategic area important to Thailand's security interests. The NSC follows China's role in the region continuously, especially in Lao PDR, Cambodia and Myanmar, including through economic and infrastructure projects, and sees a need for Thailand to have a long-term policy on how it wants the Mekong subregion to develop over the next 10–20 years.
it: China's role in the Mekong subregion and its effects on Thailand (NSC)

te: Child nutrition, Chinese investment and technology, the OECD and the Thai–Cambodian border
se: The SDG subcommittee discussed child malnutrition with the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation and the Ministry of Public Health. It comes more from the wrong nutrients than from a lack of food, and the subcommittee will make observations such as agencies working separately and the quality of school lunches and school milk. The committee also considered balancing Thai–Chinese trade by attaching conditions to foreign direct investment (FDI), such as research centres with Thai universities, noted progress in OECD cooperation such as King Prajadhipok's Institute's OECD 101 course, and followed the Thai–Cambodian border situation.
it: Child nutrition under the SDGs (Ministry of Higher Education and Ministry of Public Health)
Thai–Chinese trade balance, investment and technology upgrading
Progress on OECD membership and the Thai–Cambodian border situation

te: Following the security situation on the Thai–Cambodian border
se: The committee followed news of military equipment delivered from China to Cambodia and assessed its effects on security along the Thai–Cambodian border, as well as relations between China and Cambodia and Thailand's approach.
it: The security situation on the Thai–Cambodian border

se: The committee considered 5 international matters: the draft Plan of Action for the Thailand–Viet Nam comprehensive strategic partnership 2026–2031; the State Audit Office holding the chair and secretariat of the environmental auditing working group of the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions; the draft Dushanbe Declaration for the high-level conference on the Decade for Action “Water for Sustainable Development”; recommendations on joining ILO Conventions No. 87 and 98 and the Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families; and draft guidelines for defence cooperation on undersea infrastructure.
it: Draft Plan of Action for the Thailand–Viet Nam comprehensive strategic partnership 2026–2031
Draft Dushanbe Declaration (water for sustainable development) and ILO Conventions No. 87 and 98
Positions in an international environmental auditing working group, and guidelines on cooperation on undersea infrastructure

te: SDG 2 on farming, comparing the Thai Canal, Dawei and the Land Bridge, and state enterprises under the OECD
se: The committee discussed following SDG 2 on ending hunger and developing farming, proposing that each ministry's 5-year action plan be used to track results, and reflected structural problems of farmers such as low income, high costs and debt. It compared 3 large shipping and logistics projects: the Thai Canal, the Dawei deep-sea port and the Land Bridge, and found the Land Bridge the most feasible in terms of sovereignty, security and investment. It also discussed trade competition and the oversight of state enterprises for OECD membership with the State Enterprise Policy Office, the Board of Investment and the Trade Competition Commission, and set a seminar to present the Pink Economy report on 12 June 2026 at Parliament House.
it: Following SDG 2 and agriculture
Comparing the Thai Canal, the Dawei deep-sea port and the Land Bridge
Trade competition and state enterprise oversight under OECD guidelines
Seminar to present the Pink Economy report (12 June 2026)

te: Committee representatives for the 2027 budget committee and a background check
se: Meeting on Wednesday 6 May 2026. The committee considered its representatives in the standing committee checking the background, conduct and ethics of the person nominated as Secretary-General of the Council of State, and in the special committee studying the Annual Appropriations Bill for fiscal year 2027, naming 2 of its vice-chairs.
it: Committee representative in the background check of the nominee for Secretary-General of the Council of State
Committee representatives in the special committee on the 2027 budget bill

te: Effects of the US–Iran situation, and Thailand–China in a new world order
se: The committee followed the situation between the United States and Iran, which affects energy prices in the region, and proposed recommendations to the Senate so that Thailand, as a major food producer for the world, prepares for energy and food crises. It also considered Thailand–China in a new world order: the overall picture of East Asia, China's role towards Thailand and ASEAN, risks and opportunities for Thailand, the meaning of a “Thai–Chinese balance”, and the trade balance.
it: The US–Iran situation and its energy and food effects on Thailand
Thailand–China in a new world order and the Thai–Chinese balance

te: Report of the subcommittee on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
se: The committee heard the subcommittee following international obligations, the UN's sustainable development and international trade and economic agreements, which is studying how to drive the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in an integrated way. It invited the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Interior, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the National Economic and Social Development Council to give information, and met provincial governors and agencies in Phetchaburi, Mukdahan, Chachoengsao, Nakhon Phanom and Ubon Ratchathani, as well as making study visits.
it: The subcommittee's report on driving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
